title: boxcar audit record v1
description: One line of a session's audit log: a Record, whose `data` is shaped by its `type` as Payload lists (`type` and `data` side by side). See docs/audit-events.md.

ArtifactRef.description: A file the VMM loaded, identified by where it was and what it held.

Attrib.description: Whose identity a record carries as its `subject`.

oneOf.description: The process that made the request.
The process that opened the handle, when the request itself has no usable caller (pid 0, or a write-back from the page cache).

Checkpoint.description: `checkpoint`: a summary the log writer chains in periodically, so a reader can check a stretch of the log against one hash.

dropped.description: Droppable events that were dropped because the audit channel was full.

records_since.description: Records written since the previous checkpoint.

root_hash.description: blake3 over the raw hashes of the records since the previous checkpoint.

ControlConnect.description: `control.connect`: a process connected to the control socket. It is served (`allow`) only when its uid is the VMM's; otherwise the connection is closed before the hello (`deny`).

pid.description: The peer's process id and user id, from `SO_PEERCRED`.

ControlStop.description: `control.stop`: a control client asked the VM to stop.

open_seq.description: The `seq` of the record that opened this handle, when known.

path_at_open.description: The path when the handle was opened; differs after a rename.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

size.description: The file size at close, when it was measured.

ts_release_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_REALTIME`, nanoseconds since the epoch, when the guest released the handle: the producer's time, before the hash that completes the record, which can come a while later. 0 in logs written before it existed.

path_b64.description: `path` as base64 of its raw bytes, set when the name was not valid UTF-8 (`path` then holds the lossy form, `U+FFFD` for each bad byte); omitted otherwise.

Hash.description: A blake3 digest: `b3:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits.

HashStatus.description: Whether the content of a closed file was hashed, and if not, why.

oneOf.description: The file changed while it was being hashed.
Nothing was written through the handle, so there is nothing to hash.

dur_ms.description: How long the flow lasted, in milliseconds.

reason.description: Why it ended, such as `fin`, `rst`, `timeout`, `evicted` or `idle`.

NetConnect.description: `net.connect`: a guest connection attempt and the policy's verdict on it.

dst.description: The address and port the guest asked for.

flow.description: The flow's id, unique within the session. The flow's `net.tls` and `net.close` carry it too.

names.description: The names the guest's DNS answers gave `dst`'s address, newest first.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

src.description: The guest's address and source port.

NetDhcp.description: `net.dhcp`: the network stack answered a guest DHCP message with the session's static lease.

op.description: `offer`, the answer to a DISCOVER, or `ack`, the answer to a REQUEST.

yiaddr.description: The address the reply leases to the guest.

NetDns.description: `net.dns`: a guest DNS query, the policy's verdict on its name, and the answer the guest got.

answers.description: The addresses the answer gave, as text.

qtype.description: The query type, by its DNS number: 1 is A, 28 is AAAA.

rcode.description: The response code the guest got, by its DNS number: 0 is NOERROR, 2 SERVFAIL, 3 NXDOMAIN.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

txid.description: The transaction id the guest gave the query.

NetDrop.description: `net.drop`: the network stack dropped guest frames. Made at most once a second for each reason, counting every drop since the last.

count.description: Frames dropped for this reason since the last `net.drop` for it.

NetTls.description: `net.tls`: the gate's reading of a flow's first bytes, the name they asked for, and whether the flow was let through on it. The gate reads the flows a domain rule allowed: a TLS ClientHello's server name, or a plain HTTP request's `Host`.

alpn.description: The ALPN protocols the ClientHello offered, in its order; empty for `http`.

kind.description: What the first bytes were read as: `tls` (a ClientHello, bytes that began like one, or none at all) or `http` (anything else, read as a plain HTTP request).

sni.description: The name asked for: for `tls`, the server name the ClientHello named; for `http`, the request's `Host` (lowercase, without its port). `null` when there was none to read.

NetUdp.description: `net.udp`: the first datagram of a guest UDP flow, and the policy's verdict on it.

dst.description: The address and port the guest sent to.

flow.description: The flow's id, unique within the session (TCP and UDP flows share one count); its `net.close` carries it.

names.description: The names the guest's DNS answers gave `dst`'s address, newest first.

rule.description: The policy rule that decided, as written; `null` when the policy's default did.

src.description: The guest's address and source port.

OpResult.description: How one operation ended. Present on every filesystem event that performs an operation, so readers can filter failures without knowing the event.

err.description: The symbolic name of `errno`, such as `EACCES`, when Linux defines one.

errno.description: The Linux errno of a failure.

Payload.description:
The typed payloads: one variant per event kind this crate defines.

Adjacently tagged, so it serializes as `{"type": "fs.open", "data": {...}}`, which are the two fields a [`Record`] carries at its top level. New kinds are additive, and a consumer ignores kinds it does not know.

PolicyChanged.description: `policy.changed`: a control client replaced the session's policy (the control socket's `policy.update`): the network rules, the vsock allowlist, or both. The new policy decides every later query, connection and datagram, and what was open and it denies is closed (`net.close{reason:"policy"}`).

version.description: The policy's version from now on: 1 is the policy the VM started with, and each update adds one. `policy.get` reports it.

Record.description:
One audit record: one line of a session's log.

The JSON field names are these field names, except that `kind` is `type`. Unset optional fields are left out of the JSON, never written as `null`.

data.description: The payload. Its shape is decided by `kind`; see [`Payload`] for the kinds this crate defines.

prev.description: The `hash` of the previous record, or `genesis_prev` for the first.

seq.description: The record's position in the session, counting from 1 with no gaps. Only the log writer assigns it.

subject.description: The guest process the event is attributed to.

ts_guest_ns.description: The guest's own clock, for events reported from inside the guest. It orders ring 1 events among themselves.

ts_host_ns.description: Host wall-clock time (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, taken when the writer received the event. This is the only timestamp that joins events across rings.

ts_mono_ns.description: Host `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` in nanoseconds, taken at the same moment.

type.description: The dotted event type, such as `fs.open`.

Ring.description: Which side of the VM boundary made the record: 0 the host, 1 the guest.

SessionExit.description: `session.exit`: the session's process ended, as init reported it: its exit code, or the signal that killed it. Both are `null` only when init could not tell.

SessionId.description: A session id: a UUIDv7 in lowercase hyphenated text.

SessionStart.description: `session.start`: the guest's init started the session the VMM's config asked for. Reported by init (ring 1); the record's subject is the session's process.

argv.description: The command, as the config gave it.

pid.description: Its process id in the guest.

SetAttr.description: The attributes a `setattr` asked to change. Unset fields were not part of the request and are omitted from the JSON.

ShareRef.description: A directory the VM was given over virtio-fs.

tag.description: The share's tag, such as `root` or `workspace`.

Source.description: The component that produced a record. On the wire, the lowercase name.

oneOf.description: The guest's session, as its init reports it over the control channel.
The session's policy, as the control socket changes it.

SpanRef.description: Where an event sits in a trace.

oneOf.description: Ask the guest to end its session first.

Subject.description: The guest identity an event is attributed to.

VmmStart.description: `vmm.start`: the VM was built and is about to run.

shares.description: The virtio-fs shares, in slot order. Omitted when there are none, and read as none when absent.

console_dropped_bytes.description: Console bytes the guest wrote that the host never wrote out: the oldest bytes the console's ring dropped when the host's stdout (or the console file) fell behind, bytes a failed write lost, and what was still undelivered when the stop sequence gave up waiting for a stalled writer. 0 when the console kept up. Absent in logs written before it existed, and read as 0.

stdin_dropped_bytes.description: Bytes typed at the console that the host dropped because the guest was not reading them: the oldest input beyond what the serial FIFO and the host's 4 KiB holding buffer could take. 0 for a run with no console input. Absent in logs written before it existed, and read as 0.

VsockClose.description: `vsock.close`: a vsock connection that a `vsock.connect` let through ended.

VsockConnect.description:
`vsock.connect`: a vsock connection between the guest and the host, and whether it was let through.

A guest connection to an internal port (1024, 1025, 1026) is served by the VMM only from a guest source port below 1024, and only the first such connection to each port; a guest connection to any other port reaches the host socket `<uds>_<port>` only when the port is allowlisted. A host connection, through the vsock socket, is recorded once the guest accepts it.

peer.description: The other end: for a guest connection, `internal` (a VMM service) or `uds` (the host socket `<uds>_<port>`); for a host connection, `guest`.

port.description: The port connected to: the host port for a guest connection, the guest port for a host one.

reason.description: Why a connection was refused: `unprivileged` (an internal port from a guest source port of 1024 or more), `duplicate` (an internal port that was already connected), `no_service` (an internal port nothing serves), `port` (a port that is not allowlisted), or the reason the service at an internal port gave, such as `reactivated` (the guest control channel takes one connection in the VMM's life, and this is a later one, after the guest re-activated its vsock driver). `null` when it was let through.

src_port.description: The connecting side's port: the guest's source port, or the port the VMM gave a host connection.
